description: Canonical interpretation catalog for deterministic Augur fact artifacts.

index.meaning: Canonical manifest for deterministic artifacts produced in this run.
index.how_to_use: Use it to discover which fact artifacts exist before opening optional files.
index.what_not_to_infer: Do not treat domain presence or count alone as architecture truth.

startup.meaning: Prioritized startup subset of the deterministic artifacts for semantic orientation.
startup.how_to_use: Read this before broad repo exploration to get the recommended first-pass files.
startup.what_not_to_infer: Do not treat startup priority as a complete description of the repo.

frameworks.meaning: Normalized framework and runtime context observations.
frameworks.how_to_use: Use to understand stack and framework-shaped boundaries before naming components.
frameworks.what_not_to_infer: Framework detection does not by itself prove architecture patterns.

routes.how_to_use: Use to identify request-facing surfaces, actors, and candidate flows.
routes.what_not_to_infer: Routes alone do not define component hierarchy.

handlers.meaning: Normalized handler and entry callback observations.
handlers.how_to_use: Use to map transports and request/control entrypoints into code.
handlers.what_not_to_infer: Handler names alone are weak evidence for component ownership.

dispatch-bindings.meaning: Normalized runtime wiring and producer/consumer bindings.
dispatch-bindings.how_to_use: Use to spot routing, queue, event, and runtime registration boundaries.
dispatch-bindings.what_not_to_infer: A binding does not always correspond to a top-level component.

boundaries.how_to_use: Use to identify ports, adapters, repositories, service seams, and storage boundaries.
boundaries.what_not_to_infer: Boundary labels do not by themselves confirm higher-level concepts.

external-clients.how_to_use: Use to model external dependencies, resilience surfaces, and dependency boundaries.
external-clients.what_not_to_infer: A library import is not the same as a real runtime dependency.

config.how_to_use: Use to understand configuration flow, state sources, and mode variability.
config.what_not_to_infer: Configuration presence does not automatically make it a first-class component.

hot-files.meaning: Weighted centrality-style file ranking from deterministic signals.
hot-files.how_to_use: Use to prioritize early repo reads and breadth-pass candidates.
hot-files.what_not_to_infer: Hotness is a read-priority hint, not architecture truth.

call-edges.how_to_use: Use to support dependency direction and boundary-crossing analysis.
call-edges.what_not_to_infer: Raw function calls do not directly equal runtime architecture.

data-touches.how_to_use: Use to enrich store readers/writers, state boundaries, and config reload paths.
data-touches.what_not_to_infer: One touch does not by itself define state ownership.

execution-slices.how_to_use: Use to discover candidate flows and important execution paths.
execution-slices.what_not_to_infer: Slices are structural path hints, not final named flows.

concept-evidence.meaning: Deterministic candidate concept evidence plus run-specific review questions.
concept-evidence.how_to_use: Use to resolve concept candidates as accepted, tentative, or rejected from supporting evidence, counter evidence, evidence gaps, review questions, and repo code.
concept-evidence.what_not_to_infer: Candidate concepts are not final architecture truth.

story-seeds.meaning: Deterministic child-story planning suggestions derived from available fact domains.
story-seeds.how_to_use: Use to draft candidate child concerns before writing stories and narratives.
story-seeds.what_not_to_infer: Seeds are advisory and should not force decorative story structure.

component-seeds.meaning: Deterministic representative component slices and reading candidates derived from hot files and structural facts.
component-seeds.how_to_use: Use to choose representative entry, flow, and state or operations files for each provisional top-level component in full mode.
component-seeds.what_not_to_infer: Seeds are advisory and should not force final component boundaries without repo reading.

narrative-seeds.meaning: Deterministic ranking hints for system-overview and narrative selection.
narrative-seeds.how_to_use: Use to challenge which roots, child stories, and flow-bearing stories are worth selecting for system-overview and other teaching paths, and to decide which optional canonical narrative ids are actually justified and strongest for this repo.
narrative-seeds.what_not_to_infer: Narrative seeds are selection constraints, not final narrative truth.

health-candidates.meaning: Deterministic layered health candidates for local failures, boundary failures, and propagation scenarios.
health-candidates.how_to_use: Use to pressure health coverage and cascade reasoning before finalizing atlas health blocks.
health-candidates.what_not_to_infer: Health candidates are repair constraints and coverage hints, not final semantic truth.

symbols-seed.meaning: Deterministic exact-symbol inventory for high-signal files and component slices.
symbols-seed.how_to_use: Use to prefer exact mechanism names from code when writing findings, summaries, and flow steps.
symbols-seed.what_not_to_infer: The symbol seed is a targeted name dictionary, not a complete repo-wide symbol index.

state-seeds.meaning: Deterministic exact-name seeds for state entries grounded in state or operations files.
state-seeds.how_to_use: Use to tighten state claims around exact structs, enums, maps, config variants, and storage selectors from the grounded files.
state-seeds.what_not_to_infer: The state seeds guide naming and focus for state claims; they do not define the final storage model by themselves.

facts-guide.meaning: Run-specific interpretation guide for the deterministic artifacts present in this run.
facts-guide.how_to_use: Read this early to understand how to interpret the fact files that exist for this project.
facts-guide.what_not_to_infer: The guide explains usage; it does not replace direct code reading.

state-access-summary.meaning: Deterministic summary of component-to-store read/write access derived from normalized facts.
state-access-summary.how_to_use: Use to identify state boundaries, likely ownership, and candidate child stories around storage.
state-access-summary.what_not_to_infer: Access does not by itself prove source-of-truth status or persistence semantics.

control-hotspots.meaning: Deterministic summary of high-importance control paths and execution chokepoints derived from Joern slices.
control-hotspots.how_to_use: Use to prioritize full-mode breadth reads and candidate flow stories.
control-hotspots.what_not_to_infer: Hotspots are structural attention signals, not final component or flow names.
